contents.name: Theorem 3, Cyclic Decomposition Theorem with divisibility-ordered vector annihilators and uniqueness
contents.reason: The full cyclic-decomposition theorem is the operator form of invariant-factor decomposition and belongs on the planned page `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms`; the present page proves only the earlier cyclic-vector criterion it must supply.

contents.name: Theorem 3 Step 1, choose cyclic generators with maximal-degree conductors
contents.reason: This maximal-conductor construction is a proof component of invariant-factor decomposition, so its licensing destination is `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms`, where the full cyclic decomposition is built.

contents.name: Theorem 3 Step 2, conductor divisibility reduction by polynomial division
contents.reason: The conductor-division argument is specialized machinery for the later invariant-factor proof on `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms`; it is not needed for the primary-component proof used here.

contents.name: Theorem 3 Step 3, replace generators to obtain an independent cyclic direct sum with divisibility order
contents.reason: This step constructs the invariant-factor cyclic direct sum itself, whose named licensing page is `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms`; importing it here would duplicate that later canonical-form theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 3 Step 4, uniqueness of the cyclic annihilator sequence
contents.reason: Uniqueness of the divisibility-ordered annihilator sequence is precisely invariant-factor uniqueness, assigned to `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms`, rather than Jordan-block uniqueness proved here by ranks.

contents.name: First corollary after Theorem 3, T-admissible subspaces have invariant complements
contents.reason: The invariant-complement characterization depends on the full cyclic-decomposition theorem and is licensed by `modules-over-a-pid-and-canonical-forms`; no proof on this page requires that stronger complement result.

contents.name: Second corollary after Theorem 3, a vector realizes the minimal polynomial and T is cyclic iff minimal equals characteristic
